title.en: Present perfect: I've never seen a raven
title.sl: Present perfect: izkušnje in od kdaj
title.it: Il present perfect: esperienze e da quando
title.de: Das present perfect: Erfahrungen und seit wann

rule.en:
The present perfect joins the past to now: **have / has + the past participle**: **I've seen**, **she's climbed**, **we've been**. Regular participles end in **-ed**, like the past (climbed, walked); irregular ones must be learned (see the table): be → **been**, see → **seen**, do → **done**, go → **gone**, win → **won**.

Use it for experience in your life, often with **ever** and **never**: **Have you ever climbed Scafell Pike?** **I've never seen a raven.** Only one no: **I've never seen** (not *I haven't never seen*).

Use it for a time that started in the past and goes on now, with **since** (the starting point) and **for** (how long): **I've been here since Monday.** **We've lived here for two years.** (not *I am here since Monday*).

When you say when it happened, at a finished time, use the past simple: **I saw a raven yesterday.** (not *I've seen it yesterday*).
rule.sl:
*present perfect* poveže preteklost s sedanjostjo: **have / has + deležnik** (*past participle*): **I've seen**, **she's climbed**, **we've been**. Pravilni deležniki so na **-ed** kot preteklik (climbed, walked), nepravilne se naučimo (glej tabelo): be → **been**, see → **seen**, do → **done**, go → **gone**, win → **won**. Pomožnik je vedno have, nikoli be: bil sem → **I've been**.

Rabimo ga za izkušnje v življenju, pogosto z **ever** (kdaj) in **never** (nikoli): **Have you ever climbed Scafell Pike?** **I've never seen a raven.** (Še nikoli nisem videl krokarja.) Samo en ne: slovensko *nikoli nisem*, angleško **I've never** (ne *I haven't never*).

Rabimo ga za čas, ki se je začel v preteklosti in traja še zdaj, s **since** (od kdaj) in **for** (koliko časa): **I've been here since Monday.** (Tu sem od ponedeljka.) **We've lived here for two years.** Slovenščina tu reče sedanjik, angleščina ne: ne *I am here since Monday*.

Ko povemo, kdaj se je zgodilo, v končanem času, rabimo *past simple*: **I saw a raven yesterday.** (ne *I've seen it yesterday*).
rule.it:
Il *present perfect* collega il passato al presente: **have / has + participio passato** (*past participle*): **I've seen**, **she's climbed**, **we've been**. I participi regolari finiscono in **-ed** come il passato (climbed, walked); quelli irregolari si imparano (vedi la tabella): be → **been**, see → **seen**, do → **done**, go → **gone**, win → **won**. L'ausiliare è sempre have, mai be: sono stato → **I've been**.

Si usa per le esperienze della vita, spesso con **ever** (mai, nelle domande) e **never** (mai): **Have you ever climbed Scafell Pike?** **I've never seen a raven.** Una sola negazione: **I've never** (non *I haven't never*).

Si usa per un tempo iniziato nel passato che dura ancora, con **since** (da + un momento) e **for** (da + una durata): **I've been here since Monday.** (Sono qui da lunedì.) **We've lived here for two years.** Dove l'italiano usa presente + da, l'inglese vuole il present perfect: non *I am here since Monday*.

Se si dice quando è successo, ci vuole il *past simple*, anche dove l'italiano dice «ho visto»: **I saw a raven yesterday.**
rule.de:
Das *present perfect* verbindet Vergangenes mit dem Jetzt: **have / has + Partizip** (*past participle*): **I've seen**, **she's climbed**, **we've been**. Regelmäßige Partizipien enden auf **-ed** wie die Vergangenheit (climbed, walked); unregelmäßige lernt man: be → **been**, see → **seen**, do → **done**, go → **gone**, win → **won**. Das Hilfsverb ist immer have, nie be: ich bin gewesen → **I've been**.

Es steht für Erfahrungen im Leben, oft mit **ever** (je) und **never** (nie): **Have you ever climbed Scafell Pike?** **I've never seen a raven.** Nur eine Verneinung: **I've never** (nicht *I haven't never*).

Es steht für eine Zeit, die früher begann und bis jetzt dauert, mit **since** (seit + Zeitpunkt) und **for** (seit + Zeitdauer): **I've been here since Monday.** (Ich bin seit Montag hier.) **We've lived here for two years.** Wo das Deutsche Präsens + seit sagt, steht present perfect: nicht *I am here since Monday*.

Sagt man, wann es geschah, steht *past simple*, auch wo das Deutsche das Perfekt nimmt: **I saw a raven yesterday.** (Ich habe gestern einen Raben gesehen.)

examples.en: Poppy has never seen a raven.
examples.sl: Poppy še nikoli ni videla krokarja.
examples.it: Poppy non ha mai visto un corvo.
examples.de: Poppy hat noch nie einen Raben gesehen.

note.en: Only one no: has never seen (not hasn't never).
note.sl: Samo en ne: has never seen (slovensko nikoli ni).
note.it: Una sola negazione: has never seen (in italiano non … mai).
note.de: Nur eine Verneinung: has never seen (nicht hasn't never).

examples.en: Have you ever climbed Scafell Pike? — Yes, I have!
examples.sl: Si se že kdaj povzpel na Scafell Pike? — Ja, sem!
examples.it: Sei mai salito sullo Scafell Pike? — Sì!
examples.de: Bist du schon einmal auf den Scafell Pike gestiegen? — Ja!

note.en: ever: at any time in your life.
note.it: ever: in qualsiasi momento della vita.

note.en: since + the starting point: since Monday, since nine o'clock.
note.sl: since + začetek: since Monday, since nine o'clock.
note.it: since + il momento d'inizio: since Monday, since nine o'clock.
note.de: since + Zeitpunkt: since Monday, since nine o'clock.

examples.en: Mrs Birkett has had the inn for twenty years.
examples.sl: Gospa Birkett ima gostilno že dvajset let.
examples.it: La signora Birkett ha la locanda da vent'anni.
examples.de: Frau Birkett hat das Gasthaus seit zwanzig Jahren.

note.en: for + how long: for twenty years, for two days.
note.sl: for + koliko časa: for twenty years, for two days.
note.it: for + la durata: for twenty years, for two days.
note.de: for + Zeitdauer: for twenty years, for two days.

examples.it: Ieri Alfie ha visto un corvo.
examples.de: Alfie hat gestern einen Raben gesehen.

note.en: yesterday is finished: saw, not has seen.
note.sl: yesterday je končan čas: saw, ne has seen.
note.it: yesterday è un tempo finito: saw, non has seen.
note.de: yesterday ist vorbei: saw, nicht has seen.

examples.en: Old Wilf has lived in the dale all his life.
examples.sl: Stari Wilf že vse življenje živi v dolini.
examples.it: Il vecchio Wilf vive nella valle da tutta la vita.
examples.de: Der alte Wilf wohnt schon sein ganzes Leben im Tal.

note.en: It is still true now, so the present perfect, not the present.
note.sl: Drži še zdaj: present perfect, kjer slovenščina reče sedanjik.
note.it: Vale ancora oggi: present perfect, dove l'italiano usa il presente.
note.de: Gilt bis heute: present perfect, wo das Deutsche das Präsens nimmt.

examples.en: The sheep have been on the fell for two weeks.
examples.sl: Ovce so že dva tedna na hribu.
examples.it: Le pecore sono in montagna da due settimane.
examples.de: Die Schafe sind seit zwei Wochen auf dem Berg.
